english: I received a package.
tip: 'Mi ha detto che...' = He/she told me that... 'Dire' in passato prossimo: 'ho detto' (I said/told).

english: I brought the dessert.
tip: 'Ho avuto un'idea' = I had an idea. 'Avere' as main verb uses 'avere' as auxiliary – double avere!

english: He met a girl.
tip: 'Ci sono stato' = I've been there. 'Ci' (there) + 'essere' (stare) in passato prossimo – very common phrase.

english: We always had lunch at one.
tip: Two-verb imperfetto: 'Volevo andare al mare ma non potevo' = I wanted to go to the beach but couldn't.

english: I used to exercise every afternoon.
tip: Italian uses imperfetto more broadly than English uses 'was doing' – includes 'used to' and 'would (habitually)'.

english: Did you all listen to the music?
tip: To ask about someone's day: 'Che cosa hai fatto oggi?' = What did you do today? 'Fatto' is past participle of 'fare'.

english: They cleaned the whole house.
tip: Passato prossimo is the most-used past tense in spoken Italian – used for completed events, like English simple past.

english: We met at the bar.
tip: `ci` = 'there' (replacing a place). `Vai al cinema? Sì, ci vado` (Yes, I go there). Saves repeating the location.

english: I thought it was easier.
tip: Imperfect subjunctive after past tense main clause.

english: We got lost in the city.
tip: `ci` also gets glued to other constructions: `ci sono` (there is), `ci credo` (I believe in it). It's the small word doing a lot of work.

english: I wish it were already summer.
tip: Vorrei che + imperfect subjunctive for wishes.

english: It was very cold that night.
tip: Age expressions: 'Quando aveva vent'anni...' = When he was twenty years old... Age = state = imperfetto.

english: I didn't know what to do.
tip: 'Mi ricordo che...' (I remember that...) + imperfetto: the remembered scene is described with imperfetto.

english: I woke up late this morning.
tip: Reflexive verbs use "essere" in compound tenses, and the participle agrees: "Mi sono alzata" (f).

english: We used to read the newspaper at breakfast.
tip: 'Come stavi?' = How were you? / How were you doing? Imperfetto of 'stare' for past states of being.

english: I hated waking up early in the morning.
tip: 'Prima' (before/previously) + imperfetto: 'Prima vivevo in campagna' = I used to live in the countryside (before).

target: Non è successo niente di grave.
english: Nothing serious happened.
tip: Irregular participle: succedere→successo. Always with essere.

target: Sono stato malato tutta la settimana.
english: I was sick all week.
tip: Irregular participle: essere→stato. Always with essere.

target: Mia nonna cucinava sempre la pasta.
english: My grandmother always cooked pasta.
tip: Use imperfetto for descriptions and background: 'Era una bella giornata' = It was a beautiful day.

target: Il treno arrivava sempre in ritardo.
english: The train always arrived late.
tip: 'Succedeva spesso' (It happened often) – repeated occurrence of events = imperfetto, not passato prossimo.

target: Sempre mi dimentico di portare l'ombrello.
english: I'm always forgetting to bring my umbrella.
tip: Andare in the imperative tu-form: va' or vai.

english: Did you talk to the professor?
tip: 'È stato bello' = It was nice/beautiful. 'Stato' = past participle of both 'essere' and 'stare'.

english: They were all happy about the news.
tip: Repeated events: 'Ogni domenica, papà comprava il giornale' = Every Sunday, Dad would buy the newspaper.

target: È nato il figlio della mia amica.
english: My friend's son was born.
tip: Irregular participle: nascere→nato. Always with essere.

target: Ogni mattina prendevo il caffè al bar.
english: Every morning I had coffee at the cafe.
tip: 'Mentre' (while) triggers imperfetto: 'Mentre camminavo...' = While I was walking...

target: Mai avrei pensato di vincere questa gara.
english: I never would have thought I'd win this race.
tip: Stare in the imperative tu-form: sta'.

english: I wrote a letter.
tip: 'Fatto' (done/made), 'detto' (said), 'visto' (seen) are among the most common irregular past participles.

english: Could you repeat that, please?
tip: "Per" = for/in order to. Used for purpose (per studiare), duration (per due ore), and destination (per Roma).

english: You were right in the end.
tip: 'Non sapevo cosa dire' = I didn't know what to say. 'Sapere' in imperfetto = didn't know (ongoing state).

english: We used to live in an old building.
tip: Physical sensations: 'Avevo fame' (I was hungry), 'Avevo freddo' (I was cold). Body states = imperfetto.

english: I couldn't understand why he was angry.
tip: 'Non volevo disturbare' = I didn't want to disturb. Polite explanation for past behavior.

english: As a child I used to play in the park.
tip: The imperfetto describes ongoing or habitual past actions: 'Da bambino mangiavo sempre la pasta' = As a child I always ate pasta.

english: He used to speak five languages when he was young.
tip: Descriptions of people: 'Era alto, con gli occhi verdi' = He was tall, with green eyes. Physical traits = imperfetto.

target: Mia madre mi accompagnava a scuola.
english: My mother used to walk me to school.
tip: Weather in the past = imperfetto: 'Faceva caldo' (it was hot), 'Pioveva' (it was raining). Background conditions.

target: Da piccola giocavo sempre nel parco.
english: As a child I always played in the park.
tip: Time and age use imperfetto: 'Erano le otto' (it was 8), 'Avevo dieci anni' (I was ten years old).

target: Mia nonna cucinava la pasta ogni domenica.
english: My grandma used to cook pasta every Sunday.
tip: Imperfetto for interrupted actions: 'Dormivo quando è suonato il telefono' (I was sleeping when the phone rang).

target: Stavo guardando la TV quando hai chiamato.
english: I was watching TV when you called.
tip: Imperfetto progressivo: stavo + gerundio for action in progress.

target: Sembra che loro non capiscano il problema.
english: It seems they don't understand the problem.
tip: The subjunctive (congiuntivo) is triggered after expressions of opinion, wish, doubt, or emotion + "che".

target: È corsa a casa appena ha saputo.
english: She ran home as soon as she found out.
tip: Irregular participle: correre→corso. With essere for intransitive motion.

target: Mi alzavo presto per andare a correre.
english: I used to get up early to go running.
tip: Imperfetto: mi alzavo (alzarsi) for habitual past.

english: We were having dinner on the terrace.
tip: Imperfetto progressivo: stavamo + gerundio for action in progress.

english: My father worked in a factory.
tip: 'Stava per' + infinitive = was about to: 'Stavo per uscire quando hai chiamato' = I was about to go out when you called.

target: Non aprire la porta a nessuno.
english: Don't open the door for anyone.
tip: Negative informal imperative uses "non + infinitive": "Non parlare!" (Don't speak!). Different from positive form.

target: Aveva sempre un sorriso per tutti.
english: She always had a smile for everyone.
tip: Feelings and mental states in the past = imperfetto: 'Ero felice' (I was happy), 'Volevo partire' (I wanted to leave).

target: Giocavamo a nascondino fino a sera.
english: We played hide and seek until evening.
tip: Time and age in the past = imperfetto: 'Erano le otto' (it was 8 o'clock), 'Avevo dieci anni' (I was ten years old).

target: Da bambino avevo paura dei temporali.
english: As a child I was afraid of thunderstorms.
tip: 'Funzionava' (it worked/used to work) vs 'Ha funzionato' (it worked = completed event). Different perspective on the past.

target: Mia madre mi leggeva le fiabe.
english: My mother used to read me fairy tales.
tip: 'Mentre' (while) typically triggers imperfetto: 'Mentre camminavo...' = While I was walking... Ongoing action.

target: Quando ero giovane, vivevo in campagna.
english: When I was young, I lived in the countryside.
tip: 'Quando ero giovane...' (When I was young...) + imperfetto = nostalgic stories about the past. Very common in conversation.

target: Passavamo le sere a giocare a carte.
english: We spent the evenings playing cards.
tip: In Italian storytelling: imperfetto for the setting, passato prossimo for events. Like movie background vs action.

target: Stava dormendo quando è suonato il campanello.
english: She was sleeping when the doorbell rang.
tip: Imperfetto progressivo: stava + gerundio for action in progress.

target: Da studente dormivo sempre fino a tardi.
english: As a student I always slept in late.
tip: 'Sembrava' (it seemed) + imperfetto for appearances: 'Sembrava stanco' = He seemed/looked tired.

english: He smoked a pack a day.
tip: 'Costava poco' (It cost little) vs 'È costato poco' (It cost little). Imperfetto = general price. PP = specific purchase.

english: They fall asleep early.
tip: Reciprocal reflexives describe mutual actions: "Si amano" (They love each other). Uses plural forms.

english: Do you get enough rest?
tip: Reflexive verb: the pronoun (mi, ti, si, ci, vi) shows the action reflects back on the subject.

english: He came home exhausted.
tip: Two imperfetti together = two simultaneous ongoing actions: 'Mentre studiavo, ascoltavo musica' (While I studied, I listened to music).

english: I always thought about you.
tip: 'A quei tempi...' (In those days...) + imperfetto = describing a past era. Sets temporal background.

english: I was hoping to see you again soon.
tip: Beliefs/thoughts: 'Pensavo che fosse vero' = I thought it was true. Mental states = imperfetto.

english: He always sang in the shower.
tip: Childhood memories naturally use imperfetto: 'Mia nonna preparava sempre la torta' = My grandmother always made cake.

english: I used to start work at eight.
tip: Imperfetto describes how things were – background, habits, feelings, descriptions. Think of it as painting a picture of the past.

english: I used to go to school by bike.
tip: 'Faceva' (fare in imperfetto) covers: weather (faceva caldo), activities (faceva sport), and actions (cosa faceva?).
